subject: Clarify incident-notice scope, timelines & subproc portal onboarding
messages:
From: Olivia Morris <olivia.morris@acmehealth.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: CISO Acme <ciso@acmehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Scope & timing for incident notices - DPA obligations

Jonas,

Thanks for the quick onboarding call this morning. As we work toward finalizing the DPA and the subprocessor onboarding flow, two items need explicit clarification before our procurement team will sign:

1) Notification window and scope - the DPA currently references "prompt notice" and a 72-hour target for material incidents. We need a clear definition (e.g., "notice within 72 hours of becoming reasonably aware"), and confirmation whether that timeline applies to incidents involving a Redwood subprocessor.

2) Forensic/evidence access - our legal team requires a guaranteed path for forensic exports (slice of telemetry/affected records), an SLA for producing a forensic snapshot, and an encryption/key-handling statement for exports crossing regions.

Attached is the redline we circulated internally (acme_dpa_draft.pdf). Can you confirm Redwood's position on: 72h vs 48h windows, whether you will commit to a subprocessor notification flow, and how evidence exports are gated?

Regards,
Olivia Morris
Sr. Contracts Manager - Acme Health
[Attachment: acme_dpa_draft.pdf (PDF, 240KB)]

From: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Morris <olivia.morris@acmehealth.com>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Jul 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Scope & timing for incident notices - DPA obligations

Olivia - thanks, and appreciate the clear asks. Quick answers at a high level, with proposed next steps below. I've looped in Legal (Kimberly), Privacy Ops (Marissa), and Security (Ben) to confirm details.

High-level positions:
- Notification window: Redwood is comfortable with a contractual formulation of "notice within 72 hours of becoming reasonably aware," with an obligation to provide interim status updates if investigation is ongoing.
- Subprocessor incidents: We will extend notification obligations to incidents caused by our subprocessors where Redwood has the authority and the incident impacts customer data - and will maintain a subprocessor portal that surfaces active incidents and contact liaisons.
- Forensic exports & SLA: We can commit to producing a forensic snapshot (redacted as required) within a mutually-agreed SLA; proposing an initial 7 business-day target for a first snapshot, with priority options for expedited exports. Encryption and key handling for cross-border exports: Redwood will perform exports using customer-controlled keys where applicable; if Redwood holds keys, we propose an authenticated handoff process with audit logs.

Proposed next actions:
1) Kimberly: suggest legal clause language we can insert (attached: suggested_incident_clause.docx).
2) Marissa & Ben: confirm operational steps to onboard Acme to the subprocessor portal and the forensic export checklist (I've attached the onboarding draft).
3) Olivia: if acceptable, we'll update the DPA with the 72h notice + interim updates language and add a subprocessor notification section; we can then route for DocuSign.

I'll book 30 minutes tomorrow to walk through redline items if that helps.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Head of Legal & GTM Ops, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_portal_onboarding.docx (DOCX, 85KB)]

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Olivia Morris <olivia.morris@acmehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Jul 2028 13:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Scope & timing for incident notices - DPA obligations

Jonas / team - draft redline language below suitable for insertion into the DPA (first pass). Olivia, copying here so you can react inline.

"Incident Notification and Cooperation."
"Provider shall notify Customer of any confirmed or reasonably suspected security incident affecting Customer Data without undue delay and, in any event, within seventy-two (72) hours of Provider becoming reasonably aware of the incident. Notification shall include a description of the nature of the incident, categories of affected data, and steps taken or planned to mitigate. Provider shall provide interim updates as material facts become known and a final written incident report within thirty (30) calendar days of initial notification, subject to applicable legal constraints.

Provider's notification obligations shall extend to incidents caused by Provider's subprocessors where such incidents affect Customer Data. Provider shall maintain a Subprocessor Incident Portal for customers with active contracts and shall make designated customer liaisons available for coordination.

"Forensic Assistance and Evidence Exports."
"Provider shall, upon Customer's reasonable written request and subject to a mutually agreed scope and execution plan, produce a forensic snapshot of relevant systems and logs. Provider shall use commercially reasonable efforts to provide an initial snapshot within seven (7) business days of agreement on scope, unless otherwise agreed in writing. For cross-border evidence exports, Provider shall apply appropriate technical and organizational measures including end-to-end encryption during transit and will document key custody procedures; where Customer retains keys, Provider will coordinate export using Customer-controlled decryption.

These are suggested defaults; if Acme requires a shorter window for certain PII exposures we can table that as a carve-out in Section X.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: suggested_incident_clause.docx (DOCX, 12KB)]

From: Olivia Morris <olivia.morris@acmehealth.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: CISO Acme <ciso@acmehealth.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Jul 2028 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Scope & timing for incident notices - DPA obligations

Thanks, Kimberly and Jonas. The language looks reasonable and aligns with most of our procurement baseline. A few clarifying asks from Legal/CISO: 

- Can Redwood commit to a 48-hour notice for incidents that meet our "material exposure" definition? We can add a definition: "material exposure = confirmed unauthorized access to >1000 unique patient records or any unauthorized exfiltration of unencrypted patient identifiers."
- For the 7 business-day snapshot SLA: we need confirmation that the snapshot will include application-level logs and request traces for the affected timeframe, and that those exports will be hashed and accompanied by an integrity manifest.
- Cross-border exports: our default is customer-held keys. If Redwood needs to perform export with Redwood-held keys, we need a documented escrow/attestation process.

I've forwarded this thread to our CISO for a short note - see below.

Onward once we have the 48h carve-out decision.

Olivia

[Forwarded message]
From: CISO Acme <ciso@acmehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Jul 2028 08:58:00 -07:00
To: Olivia Morris <olivia.morris@acmehealth.com>
Subject: RE: Scope & timing for incident notices - DPA obligations

Olivia - 48h carve-out acceptable for material exposure. For export integrity: we require SHA256 manifests and signed delivery receipts. Please confirm Redwood can support these outputs.

- CISO

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Morris <olivia.morris@acmehealth.com>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 5 Jul 2028 16:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Scope & timing for incident notices - DPA obligations

Olivia / team - operations update following internal runbook review. Answers to outstanding operational asks: 

- Subprocessor portal: we can provision Acme's security contacts with read-only access to the Subprocessor Incident Portal. The portal will list active incidents, affected subsystems, and assigned liaisons. Access can be scoped to only Acme-related incidents if requested.
- 48h carve-out: we can accept a 48-hour contractual carve-out limited to the "material exposure" definition proposed; we recommend adding a cooperative investigation clause to avoid premature public disclosures.
- Forensic snapshot contents: we can include application-level logs, request traces, and relevant network flow captures for the impacted timeframe. Snapshots will be delivered as compressed, encrypted archives and paired with a SHA256 integrity manifest and a signed delivery receipt.
- SLA for snapshot: standard is 7 business days for an initial manifest and limited sample; full export turnaround depends on scope and may require additional fees for expedited processing.

Operational next steps: once DPA language is agreed, Security Ops will send the portal invite and a checklist for evidence-request scopes. Legal will add the 48h carve-out clause and the integrity manifest requirement to the DPA.

-Ben Carter
Director, Security Operations
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: evidence_export_sla.xlsx (XLSX, 16KB)]
